before.label: Clifford Geertz
before.description: Culture consists of publicly interpretable meanings. Thick description reconstructs the contexts that make actions intelligible; it is more than adding descriptive detail. “Deep Play” (1972) reads cockfighting through status and symbolic action; Negara (1980) examines ritual and political authority in nineteenth-century Bali. These are his interpretations, with their empirical reach open to debate.
before.representative_figures_and_works: The Interpretation of Cultures (1973). Weber, Wittgenstein, and Ryle are explicit interlocutors; the approach becomes influential in cultural history.
before.scope_note: Thick description interprets public, situated meanings and constrains interpretations through evidence. Hunt’s adaptation is a specific historical reception; Asad’s religion-category criticism targets a particular argument. These readings do not summarize every Indonesian or Moroccan study or establish a uniform Geertzian cultural history.

added.relationship: Levi questions fixed cultural contexts in Geertz’s interpretive practice
added.evidence_note: The 1985 essay criticizes textualization and explanatory circularity while praising Geertz’s skill. This is Levi’s specific intervention, not a verdict shared by every microhistorian.

added.relationship: Levi challenges Darnton’s use of predetermined cultural frameworks
added.evidence_note: The review targets The Great Cat Massacre’s interpretation of tales and the printers’ episode. Levi acknowledges his selective reading; neither all cultural history nor all microhistory speaks with one voice.

added.title: Giovanni Levi, “I pericoli del geertzismo,” Quaderni Storici 20/58 (1985), 269–277; consulted as “Os perigos do geertzismo,” História Social 6 (1999), 137–146, translated by Henrique Espada R. Lima Filho. DOI 10.53000/hs.n6.182.
added.citation: Giovanni Levi, “I pericoli del geertzismo,” Quaderni Storici 20/58 (1985), 269–277; consulted as “Os perigos do geertzismo,” História Social 6 (1999), 137–146, translated by Henrique Espada R. Lima Filho. DOI 10.53000/hs.n6.182.

verification.note: Complete ten-page Portuguese translation and notes read in publisher PDF. Original Italian body not collated. Technical translation review: Alessandra El Far and Fraya Frehse. Darnton quotations use the 1996 Brazilian edition, whose pages must not be assigned to the 1984 original. Supports Levi’s criticism, not an independent verdict on the books. His philosophical genealogy is partly inferred; praise of Geertz and acknowledgment of his own selective polemical reading remain explicit.

outcomes.finding: Levi’s own 1989 methodological essay and the complete published translation of his 1985 Geertzism critique now support a qualified microhistory account, rather than relying only on Ginzburg’s participant account.
outcomes.research_limit: Complete Portuguese translation of the 1985 critique read, História Social 6 (1999), 137–146, including notes; Italian body not collated. Darnton quotations use a 1996 Brazilian edition. This is evidence of Levi’s intervention, not an independent adjudication. The separate primary-method subpart reuses the complete 1989 biography essay already read in 1.40, with its existing OCR limitations; no new full-book reading claimed. Grendi’s 1977 essay remains mediated by Ginzburg. A downloaded 1993 Levi interview remains unread beyond an indexed snippet and is not cited. No philosophical influence arrows inferred from Levi’s speculative genealogy.
